Subject: Post-call recap: Private/VPC deployment - HealthTech

Hi Jared / Anita —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re all aligned and to capture next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain points and constraints
- Data residency & regulatory: certain inference workflows must remain in-country and meet PII/PHI controls.
- Air-gap required for a subset of workloads: no outbound internet egress from the inference cluster.
- Networking constraints: only private connectivity via customer transit/VPN; restricted peering and limited NAT allowed.
- Compliance: need KMS/HSM integration, audit logging, and SOC2 evidence.
- Cost/latency tradeoff: you want predictable low-latency for interactive flows while keeping unit cost under control.

Goals we heard
- POC in your environment in ~Jan 2028 to validate latency & throughput.
- Pilot (limited production) by end of Q1 2028.
- Full rollout for regulated workloads in H2 2028 with air-gapped pattern for the most sensitive models.

What Redwood can offer (high level)
- Private deployment options: VPC-hosted control plane with customer-managed VPCs, or an air-gapped on-prem package for fully offline environments.
- KMS/HSM support and audit log exports; we’ll provide SOC2 artifacts as part of enterprise onboarding.
- Recommendations for sizing and networking patterns (attached network diagram + SOW draft).

Immediate next steps
1) I’ve attached a preliminary network diagram and an SOW draft for initial sizing.
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra team + our solutions engineer (propose 11/22 or 11/29).
3) You to confirm the scope for the air-gap requirement (fully disconnected vs. restricted inbound/outbound windows).

Attachments: healthtech-network-diagram.pdf, redwood-private-vpc-sow-draft.docx

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Jared — quick answers inline below and I’ve called out where the attachments help.

> 1) Air-gap: for regulatory reasons, one business unit needs a fully air-gapped deployment (no outbound internet, strict change control). Another BU would accept restricted egress with scheduled updates. Do you have a reference architecture for both patterns?

We do. The attached network diagram includes two deployment patterns:
- Air-gapped on-prem package: full offline install that runs without outbound internet. Onboarding is done via signed artifacts (we provide signed binaries/config bundles) and we support offline updates via your change-control process. Management plane access is optional — if you require zero external management, we can ship an air-gapped control plane with offline telemetry.
- VPC-hosted/private control plane: best when you allow a private peering/VPN; control plane traffic can be restricted to your management subnet.

> 2) Sizing: for the initial POC we likely want to run on our existing VMware cluster. Do you support VMware-hosted on-prem installs or do you require bare-metal/Kubernetes?

Short answer: we support both patterns but there are tradeoffs.
- VMware: supported for POC/pilot. We’ll need guest-level GPU passthrough (vGPU or PCIe passthrough depending on your stack) and a supported driver matrix — see SOW for recommended VM footprint.
- Bare-metal/K8s: recommended for production for manageability and autoscaling.

Prelim sizing (ballpark for interactive POC): ~2 x A100 (or equivalent) to start for ~100 concurrent short-latency sessions; we’ll refine after the tech scoping call. See SOW draft for a configurable sizing table.

Next steps I’ll take now:
- Share SOW + network diagram (attached).
- Book tech deep-dive for 11/22 AM PST (provisionally).

If you can confirm the 11/22 slot I’ll loop in our solutions engineer (Lukas Meyer) and bring the deployment playbook.

Best,
Camila
